lab_supply_as_reported: 400 kHz RF generator (30 kW maximum), 17-27 kW; 21-turn coil, L = 25 uH, R = 310 mOhm
electrical_requirement: RF current in an induction coil. Torches have run from 9.6 kHz to 40 MHz at 0.5 kW to ~1 MW (PW055-V05). Coupling needs plasma radius / skin depth of ~1.5-4 (PW055-V02), so the minimum frequency falls roughly as 1/D^2: ~4 MHz for a 40 mm tube, ~0.5 MHz for >=100 mm, a 50 kHz band for >=200 mm (PW058-V02 to -V04). Lower frequency also needs more power to sustain the plasma (~1 MW at 960 Hz in argon, PW055-V04). SRC009: 80 mm tube at 400 kHz
candidate_classes: K2 (50 kW output documented at 100-400 kHz; CEIA max 100 kW is input); R1 (100-120 kW documented generators, sensitivity); R2 context only
class_used: SRC009 (400 kHz): R1 and K2 shown
eta_used: 0.91-0.96 K2 scenario at 400 kHz: 0.91 extrapolated from 1-200 kHz (PW004-V02), >0.96 claim at 100-400 kHz (PW005-V02); 0.53-0.60 R1 sensitivity; R2 not projected
industrial_unit_scale: 50 kW output at 100-400 kHz (PW006-V01); max 100 kW INPUT (PW005-V01). Patent background claims >=100 kW solid-state supplies at <=0.5 MHz (PW058-V06), not a model-specific output rating. ICP tube generators to 120 kW at 2-3 MHz (PW061-V01); VKI 1.2 MW generator rating at 400 kHz, low-pressure torch (PW056).
scale_up_constraint: Torch dimensions and operating conditions affect frequency and coupling. K2 is an industrial-heating analogue; 0.91 at 400 kHz is extrapolated and plasma-load/coil matching losses are unresolved. Larger torches can permit lower frequencies; patent examples are not universal limits.
verdict: supply choice matters and depends on torch size; large torches fall in the efficient solid-state range
